doc.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999

title: The Napoleon brothers and Uncle Phil as a child trumpeter
summary: Marty's father and uncles were all musicians, and he tells how young Phil found his father's trumpet.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: See the thing, to start it off this way, I usually start off my interviews by saying my father was the oldest of five brothers and one sister. All of the boys were professional musicians. And my father was the oldest, and he played banjo and guitar, my uncle Georgie, George Napoleon played the saxophone, my uncle Teddy was a drummer, my uncle Joey was a saxophone player — and who else, there were five brothers — Pop, Georgie, Teddy, Joey—

And Phil, right, I forgot. All musicians. Now before my uncle Phil Napoleon passed away, he called me about once every week and a half or two weeks, like that. He would call me because he wanted me to have the cemetery plots, he wanted to leave them to me

because I was the last surviving Napoleon on his side. And he would tell me stories about my father. And he said, “you know when your father was about 18 years old, 19, 18, he bought a trumpet because he wanted to play the trumpet. And he started a jazz club like I forget the name of it now, he told me what the name is I can’t remember, the Arrowsmith or the Arrow Club. And they used to chip in dues to belong to this jazz club, it was a club, you know, a society? And he said he used to put the trumpet in a closet on one of the shelves, and Phil was about five years old and he found the trumpet one day. And he started fooling with it. Next thing he was getting sounds, and my father caught him one day playing, about a year later, and he says, “I’m going to switch to guitar,” he says, or banjo, because he says, “I could never do what you’re doing.” And he was five years old. So what happened was my father used to do dates, and he would bring Phil with him on the job, at five years old. And during the course of the evening he would make an announcement about his kid brother, and put a chair in the middle of the floor, and put him on that chair and he would play the trumpet. People went absolutely bananas.
